title: More families rely on food pantries. A food drive in St. Lawrence County aims to help
summary_or_snippet: Working families in St. Lawrence County are turning more to pantries in summer. Organizers cite school-meal gaps, transportation barriers, and rising gas and food costs.
evidence_text: The article says the need really intensifies in July and August when kids don't have access to those school meal programs, and even many working families are increasingly turning to food pantries to keep food on the table. It also says local providers see transportation barriers in a very rural county like St. Lawrence, with distance between resources and access to resources, and that pantry partners have seen increases in the last couple of months as more working families rely on food pantries to supplement their budgets.
pressure_reason: The story says summer need intensifies, working families rely more on pantries, and rural transportation barriers add strain.
pressure_summary: North Country Public Radio reported that more families are relying on food pantries in St. Lawrence County as summer meal gaps, rural distance, and rising gas and food costs add pressure.
claim_supported: North Country Public Radio reported that more families are relying on food pantries in St. Lawrence County as summer meal gaps, rural distance, and rising gas and food costs add pressure.
limitations: The story reports local pantry strain and access barriers in St. Lawrence County; it does not quantify countywide unmet need.
